summary: L-5 cab built 1934 in Skagit County; abandoned 1964; Aircraft Warning Service station 1942-43; now gone, with cabin remains reported on the route.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1964 and described as gone; the Washington lookouts index marks it removed. No removal date found. Willhite's undated route notes report remains of a cabin.

access.note: On Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest land, reached by a hiking route in Willhite's notes. Public access is inferred from the land status and route notes; no closure or permit rule was found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Short hike from a large parking area at the end of a forest road, gaining about 700 feet (Willhite). Willhite's page asks visitors to call ahead because forest thinning was being planned.

events.note: L-5 cab, per the register, firelookout.com and Willhite
Activated April 6, 1942 as Aircraft Warning Service station Yoke 4-5 (Washington lookouts page)

Aircraft Warning Service station deactivated October 16, 1943 (Washington lookouts page; Willhite gives 10/16/43). The same page also gives 1944. Forest Service kept the site for fire detection afterward.
Abandoned 1964 per the register, firelookout.com and Willhite
Marked removed on the Washington lookouts index; no removal year given
Registered February 13, 2020 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Washington lookouts page gives October 16, 1943 for deactivation in one line and October 16, 1944 for the inactivation in another line that cites a May 1, 1944 report. Willhite gives 10/16/43. The timeline keeps 1943, which two sources share, and the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Sources are hobby and history sites; no official Forest Service record was read. Access 'public' is inferred from national forest land and a hiking route, not from a closure notice, so treat it as unverified. The AWS end year conflicts within the Washington lookouts page (see resolved_conflicts). No removal year is given anywhere. Willhite's route notes are undated, so the cabin remains may be old. The firetower.org photos are credited to the National Archives, but no direct image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed.
